newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia PM says interest rates coming down.
newsitem.headline: Australia PM says interest rates coming down.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Tuesday Australia's interest rates were coming down and he would like to see them lower.

"One of the reasons why interest rates have come down in Australia, and I'd like to see them still lower ... is that we are no longer running such large deficits," Howard told a Liberal Party gathering.
Howard said the government's efforts to turn the budget from a deficit to a surplus helped foster lower interest rates by reducing competition for funds.
Howard said the government was also reducing Australia's national debt and would repay A$5.0 billion off its loans in the fiscal year from July 1.
The Liberal-National government has forecast an underlying budget surplus -- excluding windfalls such as asset sales -- of A$1.6 billion for the fiscal year to June 30, 1999.
In its 1997/98 budget on May 13 this year, the government projected an underlying deficit of A$3.9 billion.
Australia's underlying budget was last in surplus -- A$402 million -- in 1990/91.
The Reserve Bank of Australia has eased monetary policy four times in less than a year, reducing official cash rates by 0.5 percentage points each time to 5.5 percent.
The most recent cut was on May 23, while the first was in July last year.
